title: Black Labrador
note: The set leader. Iterate on this one until the field colour, the light, the crop and the line weight are right — every other avatar is drawn off it. Re-declared for cool-flat-v2 on 2026-09-04: the field moved from lavender to the plaster the rooms now have (2 mention(s) rewritten); nothing else changed. Round 136 (v2) drew the circular mask into the picture — a plaster disc on a white square, corners #fefefe — so the field is now said to reach all four corners and the mask named as the app's job.
scene: Flat vector-style portrait: crisp clean edges, flat colour fills, at most two tones per surface — one light, one shadow — with no gradient between them. No airbrushing, no soft blurred shading, no photorealistic fur or fabric texture, no glossy highlights, no drop shadow, no outline heavier than a hairline. Simplified but not childish: the proportions and the anatomy stay accurate. Square 1:1. The background is one flat field of warm off-white plaster #e9e5df, edge to edge, with no gradient, no vignette, no shadow behind the subject and no texture. It is identical in every picture in this set — the twenty-four are seen side by side in a grid, and a field that drifts between them reads as a patchwork. One subject, large and centred, filling most of the frame. It is only ever seen inside a CIRCULAR MASK at small sizes, so everything that identifies the subject must sit inside the centred circle that touches the edges — nothing that matters in the corners, and no part of the head or ears clipped by that circle. Side profile facing right, head and neck only, no body and no collar. The subject is a black Labrador — matte black coat with cool grey highlights rather than glossy reflections, a broad soft muzzle, a floppy triangular ear, a modest dark-amber eye. This is the same dog the illustrations are drawn from, so give her the scruffy wire-haired beard along the jaw and chin and a small white flash at the chest. DO NOT DRAW A CIRCLE, DISC, VIGNETTE OR BORDER OF ANY KIND: the plaster field #e9e5df fills the whole square to all four corners and all four edges, and the corners are the same colour as the middle. The circular mask is applied later by the app and must not appear in the picture; a picture with white or pale corners around a drawn disc is wrong.
mustBeTrue: the background is one flat unshaded field of #e9e5df with no gradient or shadow, the rendering is flat two-tone with no airbrushing or glossy highlights, and the subject is centred and complete inside a circular mask that touches the frame edges
